clue.text: No mileage in this sect's remit? My! Strange

definitions.note: a measuring scheme based on kilometres rather than miles

indicators.note: strange letters are odd and out of order, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise that a religious sect's terms of reference contain no mention of miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges the letters of SECTSREMITMY; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: The decimal measuring scheme uses kilometres, so distances in it are never expressed in miles.

clue.text: Service for Mussolini and daughter, widely available

parts.note: Mass is a church service
pro means in favour of, for
Il Duce was Mussolini's title as Italian leader

explanation.surface: A church service is held in honour of the Italian dictator and his daughter, open to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is not a link word here: it gives PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods made in huge factory quantities are on sale everywhere, hence readily obtainable by all.

clue.text: Work hard on English fabric

parts.note: to toil is to labour hard

explanation.surface: Someone labours over a piece of English cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Toile is a linen or cotton cloth, often printed with pastoral scenes, so it is a type of material.

clue.text: Native of Russian region, beginning to go off a Spaniard?

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for the Russian native is dropped

parts.note: someone from Siberia, a vast region of Russia

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a Siberian, starting to leave, might be a Spaniard.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard comes from the Iberian peninsula, so is an example of a person from that peninsula; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: In Alaska, term for ice fan?

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Asking what Alaskans call an ice enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who glides on blades across a rink is plainly an enthusiast of frozen surfaces, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Drenches Southern trees

parts.note: oaks are trees

explanation.surface: Rain in the South soaks the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench something is to wet it thoroughly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Editor goes over uncertainty with diamonds in building

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above the next ones

parts.note: an if is a doubt or uncertainty, as in ifs and buts
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: An editor reviews a doubtful point about jewels kept in some building.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing structure, so a building in the grand sense.

clue.text: Embarrassed-looking landlord initially dismissive about your special occasion?

parts.note: an embarrassed face is red
a letter is one who lets property, a landlord

indicators.note: the opening letters of the three following words are taken

explanation.surface: A blushing landlord brushes off your big day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks as if it applies to landlord, but it governs 'dismissive about your', giving DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints' days were marked in red in church calendars, so the phrase names a memorable, notable day.

clue.text: Malicious team going around noon

indicators.note: the team word wraps round the letter for noon

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A spiteful team is circling at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Snide remarks are sneering and mean-spirited, so the word is a synonym of spiteful or malicious.

clue.text: A bad habit, grasping openings for any riches?

definitions.text: A bad habit, grasping openings for any riches?

indicators.note: the vice word clutches the initial letters inside it

parts.note: a vice is a bad habit

indicators.note: the first letters of the following two words are taken

explanation.surface: Greed is described as a bad habit that reaches out for any wealth on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes greed: a grasping vice after riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed for wealth is the classic vice described, being grasping and hungry for riches.

clue.text: Creep is awful? Exactly right!

indicators.note: the words are treated badly and their letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a creep is dreadful, and is told that is spot on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exact and accurate in every detail is spot on, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Runner, 50, by lake showing ability to perform well

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow, as on a sledge
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old runner beside a lake shows athletic talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is not an athlete but a ski, a runner that slides on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise or talent at a task is the ability to do it well, a dictionary sense.

clue.text: Where nails are available?

definitions.meaning: fingernails are located at the end of the fingers

explanation.surface: Asking where some nails might be had.
explanation.definitionFit: Nails grow at the fingertips, while the phrase also means nearby and ready for use.

clue.text: Unfriendly crowd on French island

parts.note: a host is a great crowd
ile is French for island; on places it after the crowd word

explanation.surface: An unwelcoming crowd on an island off France.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile means antagonistic or aggressive, so unfriendly in a strong sense.

clue.text: Chinese lecturer's housing of excellent quality

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, spanning the word break

explanation.surface: A Chinese academic's accommodation is first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Select goods are choice and exclusive, which is to say of the very best quality.

clue.text: Letter pile set to be rearranged

indicators.note: states outright that the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A heap of something is due to be reorganised.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as in the New Testament epistles of Paul.

clue.text: Fun in Georgia that is extremely trendy

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: the extreme first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: Enjoyment in Georgia is said to be ultra-fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaiety is merriment and light-hearted enjoyment, so fun in the noun sense.

clue.text: Surprise leading group

parts.note: up means ahead, leading, as in two goals up
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A shock result for the team that was in front.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, a shock defeat of the favourite is called an upset, so it means a surprise.

clue.text: Prepare series of carriages

definitions.meaning: to get ready by practice or coaching
a line of railway coaches coupled together

explanation.definitionFit: To coach or drill is to make ready; a locomotive with linked railway coaches is a rail vehicle of that name.

clue.text: Under discussion in answer paper

parts.note: tissue is thin soft paper

explanation.surface: Something is being debated in an exam answer paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter being debated is the point in question, the idiom for being disputed.

clue.text: Back showing no leniency

definitions.meaning: the rear part of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: The rear of a boat bears this nautical name, and a severe, strict manner is described by the same word.

clue.text: Leave one's country (not good) for this territory?

indicators.note: the letter for good is dropped from the leaving word

parts.note: to emigrate is to leave one's country to live elsewhere

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of leaving their country, which is not good, for this land.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not good)' looks like a comment on emigrating, but it removes G.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, such as those of the Gulf, so it is a territory.

clue.text: Our group impressed by Heath, say, in river

indicators.note: pressed into, so the group word is set inside the name

parts.note: Ted Heath, British Prime Minister in the 1970s, is an example of a Ted
we means our group

explanation.surface: We are impressed by Edward Heath, perhaps, beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed by' reads as admiration, but means pressed inside. Edward 'Ted' Heath was a British Conservative Prime Minister (1970-74).
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river on the border between Scotland and England.

clue.text: Very small, yet newsy — seen about

indicators.note: the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tiny item, but still newsworthy, has been spotted around.
explanation.definitionFit: This childish reduplicated word means tiny, an informal synonym for minute.
